h1: Milvus vs Elasticsearch and OpenSearch for vector search
intro: Milvus vs Elasticsearch is a question of what each system was built for: Milvus is an open-source database built for vector search, while Elasticsearch and OpenSearch are Lucene search engines that added vector fields. All three handle BM25 and hybrid search, so the real differences show up at scale: throughput, latency, index choice and cost. Choose Milvus when vector search is the core workload (RAG, semantic search, agents); keep Elasticsearch or OpenSearch when logs and analytics come first.

sections.h2: Which vector index types do Milvus, Elasticsearch and OpenSearch support?
paragraphs: Elasticsearch builds HNSW or flat indexes per Lucene segment, with int8, int4 and BBQ quantization. OpenSearch adds Faiss IVF and an on-disk mode. Milvus ships a wider menu, including GPU_CAGRA, GPU_IVF_FLAT, GPU_IVF_PQ and GPU_BRUTE_FORCE, plus scalar indexes for filters, so you can trade memory, recall and latency per field.

sections.h2: What does a purpose-built vector database add beyond vector search?
paragraphs: Elasticsearch vector search vs Milvus is a question of what the system is built around. Elasticsearch is strong when documents already live in an index. Milvus treats the collection schema as the product: typed vectors, JSON and arrays, built-in BM25 and hybrid search in the open-source build, and an architecture that scales each node role on its own.

table.caption: Milvus capabilities for vector and hybrid search workloads (milvus.io docs)
rows: Database (64 by default), collection (65,536 by default), partition (1,024 per collection), or partition key for millions of tenants
JSON fields with JSON path indexes; a dynamic field stores undeclared keys
Typed arrays, ARRAY_CONTAINS filters, BITMAP or INVERTED indexes
Up to 10 vector fields; hybrid_search fuses dense, sparse and BM25 with RRF or weighted rerankers
A BM25 function with standard, english, chinese, ICU or custom analyzers; query with raw text
TEXT_MATCH and PHRASE_MATCH (with slop) on analyzed VARCHAR fields
LIKE and RE2 regex (=~, !~), accelerated by an NGRAM index
upsert with partial_update=True; collection.ttl.seconds expires entities
Query, streaming and data nodes over shared object storage, scaled independently
Hot data loads on demand and cold data is evicted, so query nodes hold less in memory

sections.h2: How do Elasticsearch and OpenSearch fields map to a Milvus schema?
paragraphs: Most mappings translate one to one. Text fields become analyzed VARCHAR with a BM25 function, so keyword relevance survives the move. Milvus docs also map the query DSL: match to full-text search, term to == or TEXT_MATCH, prefix and wildcard to LIKE, knn to search, and RRF to hybrid_search.

table.caption: Elasticsearch to Milvus field mapping for migration
rows: VARCHAR or INT64 primary key; keep the same ID for dual-write
FLOAT_VECTOR (or FLOAT16, BFLOAT16, INT8) with the same dimension and metric
VARCHAR with enable_analyzer + BM25 function to SPARSE_FLOAT_VECTOR
VARCHAR with INVERTED or BITMAP index; NGRAM for wildcard
INT64 / DOUBLE with STL_SORT or INVERTED index
JSON field with JSON path indexes, or the dynamic field

sections.h2: How do you migrate from Elasticsearch or OpenSearch to Milvus?
paragraphs: Move the retrieval path first and keep the old cluster serving until results match. VTS (Vector Transport Service) lists Elasticsearch as a source connector; for OpenSearch, export with the scroll API and load files with BulkWriter.
bullets: Export: VTS es_to_milvus, or scroll / point-in-time reads of _source.
Create the schema: map fields, add a BM25 function, index filter fields.
Backfill with BulkWriter and bulk_import; use insert for small sets.
Dual-write new documents to both systems from the same source.
Validate recall and relevance on a query set, then shift reads gradually.

sections.h2: When do Elasticsearch or OpenSearch fit better?
paragraphs: A fair call: if search is a side feature of an existing Elastic stack, adding vectors there can be enough.
bullets: Logs, observability and security analytics built on Kibana or OpenSearch Dashboards.
Aggregation-heavy analytics and faceting over text, with vectors as a small add-on.
An existing ELK pipeline where a modest vector corpus does not justify a second system.

code.h2: How do you map an Elasticsearch index to a Milvus collection in Python?
code.intro: This script reads every document from an Elasticsearch index and writes it into a Milvus collection with dense, BM25, keyword, array and JSON fields.
code.code:
# pip install -U pymilvus elasticsearch
from elasticsearch import Elasticsearch, helpers
from pymilvus import MilvusClient, DataType, Function, FunctionType

es = Elasticsearch("http://localhost:9200")
client = MilvusClient(uri="http://localhost:19530")

# ES mapping: title(text) category(keyword) tags(keyword[]) attrs(object) embedding(dense_vector, 768)
schema = client.create_schema(enable_dynamic_field=True)
schema.add_field("id", DataType.VARCHAR, is_primary=True, max_length=64)  # ES _id
schema.add_field("title", DataType.VARCHAR, max_length=8192, enable_analyzer=True, enable_match=True)
schema.add_field("title_bm25", DataType.SPARSE_FLOAT_VECTOR)  # filled by the BM25 function
schema.add_field("category", DataType.VARCHAR, max_length=128)
schema.add_field("tags", DataType.ARRAY, element_type=DataType.VARCHAR, max_capacity=64, max_length=128)
schema.add_field("attrs", DataType.JSON, nullable=True)
schema.add_field("embedding", DataType.FLOAT_VECTOR, dim=768)
schema.add_function(Function(name="title_bm25_fn", function_type=FunctionType.BM25,
                             input_field_names=["title"], output_field_names=["title_bm25"]))

idx = client.prepare_index_params()
idx.add_index(field_name="embedding", index_type="HNSW", metric_type="COSINE",
              params={"M": 16, "efConstruction": 200})
idx.add_index(field_name="title_bm25", index_type="SPARSE_INVERTED_INDEX", metric_type="BM25")
idx.add_index(field_name="category", index_type="INVERTED")
idx.add_index(field_name="attrs", index_type="INVERTED", index_name="attrs_brand",
              params={"json_path": 'attrs["brand"]', "json_cast_type": "varchar"})
client.create_collection("docs", schema=schema, index_params=idx)

batch = []
for hit in helpers.scan(es, index="docs", query={"query": {"match_all": {}}}):
    src = hit["_source"]
    batch.append({"id": hit["_id"], "title": src["title"], "category": src["category"],
                  "tags": src.get("tags", []), "attrs": src.get("attrs"),
                  "embedding": src["embedding"]})
    if len(batch) == 1000:
        client.insert("docs", batch)
        batch = []
if batch:
    client.insert("docs", batch)
code.note: Match dim and metric_type to your dense_vector mapping. For large indexes, write files with BulkWriter and load them with bulk_import instead of insert. Code requires a running server and your own embedding model; it is an example, not a benchmark.

faqs: You can use Elasticsearch as a vector database, but it is a search engine with vector fields: dense_vector stores embeddings and the knn query searches HNSW or flat indexes per Lucene segment. Milvus is a database built around vector indexes, with BM25 and filtering added on the same collection.
Is Milvus faster than Elasticsearch for vector search?

On the VectorDBBench Cohere 1M test, Milvus-16c64g-sq4u-fp16-force_merge lists 9,575.69 QPS at 0.9189 recall and ElasticCloud-8c60g-force_merge 2,353.89 QPS at 0.9143. Hardware differs by row; benchmark your own data.
Can Milvus replace Elasticsearch for BM25 full-text search?

For retrieval, yes: a BM25 function turns analyzed text into a sparse vector at insert time, and you query with raw text, alone or in hybrid search. Kibana dashboards and aggregation-heavy analytics stay with Elasticsearch.
How does hybrid search work in Elasticsearch vs Milvus?

Elasticsearch fuses BM25 and kNN with the reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) retriever, which Elastic lists under the Enterprise subscription. OpenSearch uses search-pipeline processors. Milvus runs hybrid_search with RRFRanker or WeightedRanker in the open-source build.
How do I migrate dense_vector data from Elasticsearch to Milvus?
Map dense_vector to FLOAT_VECTOR with the same dimension and metric, then copy data with VTS or a scroll export plus BulkWriter. Dual-write during cutover and compare recall before moving reads.
Should I run Milvus and Elasticsearch together?

Often, yes. Running Elasticsearch and Milvus side by side is common: keep Elasticsearch for logs and analytics, move vector and hybrid retrieval to Milvus, feed both from the same source, and join results by document ID.
